items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But it was in Detroit where I sat in with him, same club.

ctx.x: I used to go down to the playground. It was right near that bar, the Spokane Bar, where I was trying to sell papers and nobody would listen. The jukebox was loud. On that same street, a block down, was a playground. It was brand new. I was on my way back from there, and I ran into two guys. One of them I knew. They were men, and I was just a kid. One of them I knew, because he was the director at the center that I used to play games at. I used to shoot pool there, and basketball and all that stuff was played…
was not too long after that he lost his life in Detroit. But it was in Detroit where I sat in with him, same club.
You mentioned your father – your stepfather making you a guitar.
